real_task: Evaluate whether pre-tree blob-OID comparison prevented an incorrect remote tree during Session 092's real connector publication, and whether the result can honestly be attributed to publish-manifest rather than native Git alone.
observed_problem: Session 026 created one wrong blob and one wrong tree before final-tree comparison detected truncation. Session 092 encountered the same natural failure mode after DEC-0018.
problem_trace: docs/SESSIONS.md Sessions 026 and 092, lab/observations/2026-10-02-publish-manifest-plan.json, and the Session 092 connector transcript.
baseline: Session 026 final-tree-only verification: 1 incorrect remote tree was created before the blob mismatch was localized.
hypothesis: Comparing every returned blob OID with the tested local OID before create_tree reduces incorrect remote trees created before detection from 1 to 0 while final tree equality remains true.
metric: incorrect remote trees created before blob-mismatch detection
minimum_useful_effect: Reduce the observed count by at least 1, from 1 to 0, with the final published tree equal to the tested local tree.
quality_control: Preserve exact expected, rejected and corrected blob OIDs plus final tree IDs; confirm operation ordering from the transcript; run publish-manifest only as a post-hoc correctness replay. If the CLI was not used during the field intervention, do not credit it with the field result.
overhead: Include startup, trace reconstruction, one post-hoc manifest invocation, documentation, LAB tests, checkpoint refresh and publication. The metric does not imply time or token savings.
stop_condition: Stop after comparing the two real publications and classifying attribution. Do not change publish-manifest, add preflight code, recreate a bad tree or automate connector writes.
decision_reason: The real pre-tree OID check reduced incorrect trees before mismatch detection from 1 to 0 and preserved exact final-tree equality. Keep the documented practice and final tree check. The field run used native Git IDs, so it does not establish incremental utility for the publish-manifest CLI and justifies no code extension.
failures: The first Session 092 transfer of docs/SESSIONS.md was truncated and returned the wrong blob OID; the check stopped before create_tree.

The first post-hoc extraction guessed a nonexistent `changes` key instead of the documented `entries` key and raised KeyError; reading the actual JSON fixed the inspection without changing the result.
limitations: The comparison spans two sessions with different file sizes, output caps and agent/runtime state. It measures immutable objects created before detection, not time, tokens or general agent quality. Session 092 used native git rev-parse object IDs rather than publish-manifest, so the CLI remains correctness-replayed but field-utility-uncredited.
